subject: Medford and West Medford Square Zoning Updates
overview: The Community Development Board and city planners held a public information session to present proposed zoning changes for Medford Square, West Medford Square, and Accessory Dwelling Unit regulations. The session reviewed proposed density increases, building height transitions, and the upcoming timeline for formal public hearings.

items.title: Introduction and Staff Presentation
items.summary: Planning Director Alicia Hunt introduced the project team and consultants tasked with aligning city zoning with the 2023 Comprehensive Plan.

items.title: Zoning Process and Timeline
items.summary: Consultant Paula Ramos Martinez outlined the four-step approval process involving the City Council and the Community Development Board.

items.title: Medford Square Zoning Framework
items.summary: The board reviewed a framework for mixed-use districts in Medford Square, proposing height limits ranging from four stories by right to 12 stories with incentive zoning near Interstate 93.

items.title: Development Protections and Standards
items.summary: The proposal includes 45-degree height transitions and daylight standards to protect existing residential neighborhoods abutting commercial developments.

items.title: West Medford Square Zoning Proposal
items.summary: The plan for West Medford Square maintains intensity along High Street and the rail tracks while transitioning to three-story limits in surrounding residential areas.

items.title: Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) Regulations
items.summary: Staff presented updates to bring the city into compliance with new state laws regarding protected ADUs, including size caps of 900 square feet and parking exemptions near transit.

items.title: Interactive Mapping Tool Introduction
items.summary: The city introduced a public GIS tool allowing residents to view current conditions and proposed zoning changes on a parcel-by-parcel basis.

items.title: Public Comment: ADU Feasibility and Permitting
items.summary: Residents inquired about basement conversions, parking mandates, and whether the Community Development Board or Zoning Board of Appeals would grant special permits.

items.title: Public Comment: Neighborhood Character and Outreach
items.summary: Community members expressed concern regarding the sufficiency of public notifications and the potential loss of neighborhood character due to increased density.

items.title: Public Comment: Storefront Vacancy and Maintenance
items.summary: The board discussed strategies for addressing vacant storefronts and encouraging property maintenance among non-responsive commercial landlords in West Medford.

items.title: Public Comment: Infrastructure and Traffic
items.summary: Discussion focused on the fiscal challenges of converting private ways to public streets and the use of developer linkage fees to mitigate traffic impacts.

items.title: Historic Review and Future Procedures
items.summary: Officials confirmed that new zoning does not abolish Historical Commission review for homes older than 75 years and outlined the next public hearings scheduled for late May and early June.
